transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, hi. I guess what brings me in is… it sounds a little silly, but at school, if I see balloons—even just across the hallway—my chest tightens right away and I kind of freeze for a second. It takes me a moment before I can think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing. I know that probably sounds odd.
Are you afraid that a balloon might pop when you see one?

Yes… I think that’s it. I know it’s probably just decoration, especially in a classroom, and I feel a little embarrassed saying it. But if I see one that looks really stretched tight, or it’s bobbing around near the kids, my mind goes right to, “What if it bursts right in front of me?” And I get scared in a way that feels… bigger than it should be, I guess.
Is your fear mainly just about balloons?

Mostly, yes… I mean, I know a balloon in the classroom is probably just decoration, and it’s not like I think every balloon is dangerous. But when one looks really stretched tight, or it’s bobbing around near the children, I immediately think it could burst right in my face. And then I get scared in a way that feels kind of… too big for the situation, if that makes sense.
Other than balloons, are there any other things or situations that cause this same kind of fear for you?

Um… not really, I don’t think so. I mean, loud sudden noises aren’t my favorite, but it’s really the balloon thing that stands out. I haven’t noticed the same kind of reaction with other situations. Does that make sense?
Do you go out of your way to avoid balloons?

A little, yes… I mean, I try not to make it a big thing. But lately I’ve been asking my aides to handle birthday circles if there are balloons involved, and at festivals or school events I’ll sort of… drift away from tables that have balloons nearby. If I absolutely have to stay, I keep my distance and try not to look at them, just focus on getting through it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
